template_name: Identify the Contracting Parties and Legal Capacity
description: Determines which persons or entities are bound by an agreement and whether an apparent intermediary acted as principal, agent, partner, lender, investor, or service provider.
application_scenario: Use when the existence of a transaction is accepted but the parties dispute who contracted with whom or how their relationship should be legally characterized.
reasoning_flow: List each plausible contracting party and the legal capacity attributed to that party.
Examine communications, forms, invoices, payment arrangements, delivery conduct, and prior dealings for objective indications of assent and capacity.
Distinguish conduct performed on a party's own account from conduct performed for a disclosed or undisclosed principal.
Characterize the transaction according to its substance rather than the label later assigned by either side.
Identify which obligations, payment rights, and liabilities follow from the resulting party structure.
example_application: A customer deals through an intermediary who uses another company's form. Determine whether the intermediary contracted personally or merely arranged performance for another entity before assessing payment liability.

template_name: Reconstruct Express and Implied Contractual Obligations
description: Reconstructs the operative obligations of the parties from written terms, oral communications, commercial context, and necessary implications.
application_scenario: Use when liability depends on the content of an incomplete, informal, oral, or disputed agreement, including timing, payment, cooperation, information, delivery, or completion obligations.
reasoning_flow: Collect the documents, communications, and conduct that record or evidence the agreement.
Separate express promises from background expectations and post-contract assertions.
Determine whether any additional term must be implied to make the arrangement workable or reflect an established course of dealing.
Specify each obligation, the party responsible, the required performance, and any deadline or condition.
Use the reconstructed obligation set as the baseline for later breach, payment, termination, and remedy analysis.
example_application: A business-transfer agreement requires cooperation but does not fully describe the information to be supplied. Identify the express duties and any necessary implied duty to provide materials essential to completion.

template_name: Determine Whether Performance Amounted to Contractual Breach
description: Tests alleged conduct against the operative contractual obligations to determine whether there was nonperformance, defective performance, delay, abandonment, or repudiatory conduct.
application_scenario: Use when one party alleges failure to deliver goods, complete services, provide required information, make payment, cooperate, or otherwise perform an agreed obligation.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise obligation said to have been broken.
Determine when and how performance became due, including any relevant sequence or dependency between obligations.
Compare the required performance with the acts actually completed, omitted, delayed, or refused.
Assess whether any contractual excuse, condition, prevention by the other party, or accepted variation alters the performance standard.
Classify the failure by type and materiality so that downstream termination and remedy questions can be evaluated.
example_application: A supplier accepts a payment instrument but does not complete delivery. Compare the agreed payment-and-delivery sequence with the parties' conduct and classify any failure before assessing remedies.

template_name: Assess a Right to Suspend or Withhold Payment
description: Determines whether a party may delay or withhold money that would otherwise be payable because of an express condition, a genuine contingent liability, incomplete performance, or another recognized basis.
application_scenario: Use when a payer admits receiving value or funds but argues that payment is not yet due or may be retained pending another event.
reasoning_flow: Establish the amount or performance that would ordinarily trigger payment.
Identify the clause or doctrine relied on to postpone, suspend, retain, or set off payment.
Interpret whether the asserted event is a true condition precedent, a timing mechanism, a security measure, or merely a commercial concern.
Check whether the triggering contingency has actually occurred or is supported by concrete evidence rather than speculation.
Determine the portion, if any, that remains presently payable after applying the valid condition or adjustment.
example_application: A contractor receives money attributable to a subcontractor's completed work but retains it because a third party might later seek repayment. Determine whether the contract makes that possibility a valid condition for withholding.

template_name: Evaluate Contract Termination or Rescission Following Breach
description: Determines whether an alleged breach entitled the innocent party to terminate or rescind and whether the termination procedure and timing were legally effective.
application_scenario: Use when parties dispute who ended the agreement, whether a prior breach justified that step, or whether notice and election requirements were satisfied.
reasoning_flow: Identify the breach relied on as the basis for ending the agreement.
Assess whether the term breached or the consequences of the breach were sufficiently serious to justify termination or rescission.
Determine when the terminating party learned of the relevant facts and whether it clearly elected to end the contract.
Check compliance with contractual notice, cure, deadline, and communication requirements.
Separate obligations and remedies that accrued before termination from those affected by the termination itself.
example_application: A purchaser ends a transaction after repeated failures to provide completion materials. Determine whether those failures were sufficiently serious and whether the purchaser gave an effective notice of termination.

template_name: Test Affirmation, Waiver, or Loss of a Contractual Objection
description: Assesses whether a party that knew of a defect, misrepresentation, or breach nevertheless continued the contract in a manner that limits a later attempt to avoid liability.
application_scenario: Use when a party relies on an earlier defect but subsequently performed, accepted benefits, made payments, or otherwise treated the agreement as continuing.
reasoning_flow: Identify the defect, breach, or representation on which the later objection is based.
Determine when the objecting party obtained sufficient knowledge of the relevant facts.
Review subsequent conduct for continued performance, acceptance of benefits, payment, delay, or express confirmation.
Distinguish a temporary reservation of rights from an unequivocal election to continue the agreement.
Determine which objections or remedies remain available after accounting for affirmation, waiver, or reliance by the other party.
example_application: A contracting party learns of an alleged misrepresentation but continues working under the agreement. Evaluate whether that conduct preserved or relinquished the later attempt to avoid the contract.

description: Calculates the net amount presently due by reconciling the agreed price, additional authorized work, invoices, payments, credits, and legally available deductions.
application_scenario: Use when liability for some payment is established or largely uncontested but the amount due remains disputed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the contractual price or other primary monetary obligation.
Add charges for variations, additional work, goods, interest, or expenses only where authorization and contractual entitlement are established.
Match invoices and payment demands to the underlying work or goods.
Deduct proven payments, refunds, credits, agreed allowances, and valid set-offs without double counting.
Present the net balance and separately flag any component that depends on unresolved entitlement or evidence.
example_application: A service provider completed the original scope and additional approved work, while the customer made several partial payments. Reconcile the contractual charges and credits to determine the remaining balance.

template_name: Determine Whether a Later Transaction Discharged an Earlier Obligation
description: Determines whether a later payment, asset transfer, compromise, forfeiture, or settlement extinguished or modified an earlier debt or contractual claim.
application_scenario: Use when the parties agree that a later transaction occurred but dispute whether it was partial performance, collateral security, a separate transaction, or a full settlement.
reasoning_flow: Define the earlier obligation and the amount or performance then outstanding.
Identify the later transaction and the consideration exchanged.
Examine contemporaneous words and conduct for an objective intention to settle, substitute, secure, or partially satisfy the earlier obligation.
Check whether the alleged discharge satisfies any legal requirements for compromise, variation, or acceptance of substituted performance.
Allocate the later transaction as full discharge, partial credit, security, or a separate dealing for subsequent remedy analysis.
example_application: A debtor transfers an interest in property after receiving a loan. Determine whether the transfer was accepted as complete settlement, as partial repayment, or merely as security.

description: Measures the monetary position the claimant would have occupied if the contract had been properly performed, while excluding unsupported or guaranteed returns that were never promised.
application_scenario: Use after breach is established and the claimed loss concerns a missed purchase, resale margin, expected profit, or other contractual bargain.
reasoning_flow: Define the promised performance and the economic position expected on proper completion.
Select the legally relevant valuation point and a reliable measure such as market value, replacement cost, contract price differential, or provable net profit.
Deduct sums recovered, retained, refunded, or avoided because performance did not occur.
Distinguish a contractually protected expectation from a speculative projection or non-guaranteed profit.
State the recoverable loss components separately from interest, costs, and other ancillary relief.
example_application: A buyer loses a completed purchase after paying the price. Compare the contract price with reliable market evidence at the relevant time, then deduct money recovered or expenses avoided.

template_name: Analyze Causation, Mitigation, and Consequential Loss
description: Tests whether claimed secondary losses were caused by the breach, were reasonably foreseeable, and were reduced through reasonable substitute action.
application_scenario: Use when a claimant seeks costs or losses beyond the direct contract price, such as replacement work, delay exposure, freight, demurrage, or downstream liability.
reasoning_flow: Identify each claimed loss and the breach alleged to have produced it.
Construct the factual sequence linking the breach to the claimed consequence and identify any independent intervening cause.
Assess whether the type of loss was within the parties' reasonable contemplation when contracting.
Review the claimant's response for reasonable steps to obtain substitute performance, limit delay, recover value, or avoid additional expense.
Deduct avoided loss and separate recoverable mitigation expenditure from excessive, speculative, or unrelated costs.
example_application: A contractor abandons specialized work, requiring replacement work and causing delay under a connected project. Trace the causal link, assess foreseeability, and evaluate whether the replacement response was reasonable.
